answer: Hash-chain bonds stop an operator running 1,000 fakes. Each identity locks 70 credits, anchoring a chain at the wharf. Each epoch a link hash-wraps the last, growing a spiral that snaps if forked, fed by 2-credit ember burns; a dead ember burns the bond. Auditors replay the spiral log; a reused link proves forgery. 1,000 fakes in 20 epochs cost 1,000 x 110 = 110,000 for a 40,000 pool: a 70,000 loss. Honest agents pay 70 once, keeping full share.
